content: 1. The document titled Health Facility Data: Guidance for RMNCAH Programme Managers provides detailed instructions for managing health facility data, specifically tailored for reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health (RMNCAH) programs. This document was accessed on September 18, 2020. 2. Barreix M, Lawrie TA, Kidula N, Tall FB, Bucagu M, Chahar R, and colleagues developed the WHO Antenatal Care Recommendations Adaptation Toolkit. This toolkit offers a standardized approach for countries to adapt antenatal care guidelines effectively. The publication appeared in Health Research Policy and Systems in 2020 (Volume 18, Article 70) and can be accessed via DOI: 10.1186/s12961-020-00554-4. 3. The National eHealth Strategy Toolkit provides a comprehensive framework for countries to develop and implement eHealth strategies. This resource was accessed on September 18, 2020. 4. A background document supporting the 2018 joint statement by WHO, UNFPA, UNICEF, ICM, ICN, FIGO, and IPA defines competent maternal and newborn health professionals. It outlines the qualifications and skills required for health personnel providing care during childbirth. This document was accessed on June 14, 2019. 5. WHO's OptimizeMNH recommendations focus on optimizing health worker roles to improve access to essential maternal and newborn health interventions through task shifting. This resource was accessed on January 10, 2019. 6. The document Classifying Health Workers: Mapping Occupations to the International Standard Classification provides a framework for categorizing health workers. It was accessed on September 18, 2020. 7. Downie S, Finlayson K, Tunçalp Ö, and Gülmezoglu AM conducted a scoping review titled What Matters to Women, which identifies the processes and outcomes of antenatal care that are important to healthy pregnant women. This study was published in BJOG in 2016 (Volume 123, Issue 4, Pages 529–539). 8. The CAMUNDA DMN tutorial provides guidance on decision modeling and notation (DMN) for healthcare applications. 9. The third edition of Pregnancy, Childbirth, Postpartum, and Newborn Care: A Guide for Essential Practice serves as a comprehensive reference for healthcare providers. This guide was accessed on October 8, 2020. 10. WHO's Adolescent Job Aid is a practical desk reference tool designed for primary-level health workers to address adolescent health needs. This resource was accessed on December 21, 2020. 11. WHO, UNFPA, and UNICEF published the second edition of Managing Complications in Pregnancy and Childbirth: A Guide for Midwives and Doctors, which is part of the Integrated Management of Pregnancy and Childbirth (IMPAC) series. This guide was accessed on October 13, 2020. 12. WHO's consolidated guideline on self-care interventions for health, focusing on sexual and reproductive health and rights, provides evidence-based recommendations. This guideline was accessed on December 17, 2020. 13. The Consolidated Guidelines on HIV Testing Services emphasize the 5 Cs: consent, confidentiality, counseling, correct results, and connection. This document was accessed on October 14, 2020. 14. WHO's guidelines on hepatitis B and C testing provide recommendations for screening and diagnosis. This resource was accessed on October 13, 2020. 15. WHO's guideline on syphilis screening and treatment for pregnant women offers evidence-based recommendations to improve maternal and newborn health outcomes. This guideline was accessed on October 14, 2020. 16. The Consolidated Guideline on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights of Women Living with HIV provides comprehensive recommendations for addressing the unique needs of this population. This document was accessed on December 17, 2020. 17. WHO's recommendations for the prevention and treatment of pre-eclampsia and eclampsia provide evidence-based guidance for managing these conditions. This resource was accessed on October 14, 2020. 18. The WHO position paper on influenza vaccines, published in November 2012, outlines the organization's stance on immunization against influenza. 19. The Maternal Immunization Against Tetanus guide, part of the Integrated Management of Pregnancy and Childbirth (IMPAC) series, provides recommendations for preventing neonatal tetanus. This document was accessed on November 20, 2020. 20. This guideline was accessed on October 14, 2020. 21. The fifth edition of Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use, a cornerstone of WHO's family planning resources, provides evidence-based guidance on contraceptive use. This document was accessed on December 17, 2020. 22. WHO's 2015 recommendations on health promotion interventions for maternal and newborn health provide strategies to improve outcomes through targeted health promotion activities. This resource was accessed on October 14, 2020. 23. WHO, UN Women, and UNFPA published a clinical handbook titled Healthcare for Women Subjected to Intimate Partner Violence or Sexual Violence, offering practical guidance for healthcare providers. This document was accessed on October 14, 2020. 24. WHO's 2013 clinical and policy guidelines on responding to intimate partner violence and sexual violence against women provide evidence-based recommendations for healthcare providers. This resource was accessed on October 14, 2020. 25. The Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission of Syphilis guide, part of the Integrated Management of Pregnancy and Childbirth (IMPAC) series, outlines strategies to eliminate congenital syphilis. This document was accessed on December 17, 2020. 26. Lattof SR, Moran AC, Kidula N, Moller AB, Jayathilaka CA, Diaz T, and colleagues developed a monitoring framework for implementing WHO's new antenatal care model, which aims to provide a positive pregnancy experience. This study was published in BMJ Global Health in 2020 (Volume 5, Article e002605). 27. The Key Terms and Theory of Change working group developed a consensus definition of digital health, which was presented in a digital health and interoperability presentation. This resource was accessed on February 18, 2020. 28. The guide Developing Health Management Information Systems: A Practical Guide for Developing Countries provides a framework for establishing effective health information systems. This document was accessed on October 8, 2020. 29. The Australian Digital Health Agency provides resources on clinical terminology to support the implementation of digital health systems. 30. The International Classification of Diseases (ICD) Information Sheet offers an overview of the ICD system for classifying diseases and health conditions. This resource was accessed on October 8, 2020. 31. HL7's FHIR Release 4 provides detailed information on data types used in healthcare interoperability standards.
